co_slabulous.blurb: Slabulous is a small slab buttress tucked just west of the Devil's Gate wall in the Devil's Head area of the South Platte, sitting around 9,300 feet. Ten routes, nine of them bolted and one on gear, run from 5.6 up to 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.9 range. That makes it the gentle companion to the much harder wall below, a good pick for newer leaders or a mellow day. The granite here is climbed on low-angle faces rather than steep walls, and the tops of the lines are said to give wide views over the surrounding hills.

co_well_dunn_wall.blurb: Well-Dunn Wall is a compact cave in Rifle Mountain Park, set on a small rise above the Wicked Cave. It holds ten sport lines on very steep limestone, around forty feet long, with powerful moves between small pockets. Grades are hard: most sit around 5.13, with a couple of 5.12s and a pair reaching 5.14. Expect rock that is chossy in places, so loose stone and dust are part of the deal, and many lines are seldom repeated and may need a brush. The cave catches morning sun, tends to be humid and buggy, and can seep after heavy rain.

co_superchief_boulder.blurb: Superchief Boulder is a single block within the Freight Yard Boulder Area, in Unaweep Canyon on the Grand Junction side, close to a cement factory and a little over a mile from the junction of US 50 and CO 141. Ten problems cover V1 to V8, but the bulk cluster right at V4, so it suits climbers who already boulder in the middle grades. The boulder is praised for its quality lines over flat, friendly landings.
co_superchief_boulder.approach: Off the dirt road to the factory, climb the slope on the factory's right side to the boulder.

co_warm_up_blocks.blurb: The Warm-Up Blocks are a pair of good-sized boulders in the Big Elk Meadows boulders, in the St. Vrain canyons near Lyons. They are the closest bouldering to the pullout, so the effort to reach them is tiny. Ten problems range from V1 up to about V8, most between V2 and V5 with a few harder ones, and the landings are good. Locals note the blocks look better than they climb, and some problems stay shaded most of the day, which helps on warm afternoons. A handy first stop before moving on to bigger boulders nearby.
co_warm_up_blocks.approach: The blocks stand directly across the road from the parking pullout, a very short walk.
